_README: Canonical bench registry for this machine. ONE copy, at
C:/dev/qmx-panadapter/tools/bench.json - every worktree reads it by
absolute path. Never copy it into another tree; edit it here.
Paths use forward slashes deliberately: PowerShell accepts them and it
keeps this file free of backslash escaping.
Runtime state (who holds the build lock, who holds the antenna) lives in
the lock file, NOT here. This file is the plan; the lock is the moment.

antenna.note: One antenna, two radios, a 2-way switch. Only ONE bench is on air at a time. The spare switch position feeds a dummy load, so a TX on the off-antenna bench is safe. Record the holder with 'bench antenna <name>' - decode counts and noise floor from the antenna-less bench are meaningless.

benches.name: dev
benches.role: Reclaimed 2026-09-04 for main - Randy/Dirk groups.io feedback fixes. Track A (feat/rx-audio-output) loan interrupted; put it back once verified.
role_note: This bench normally runs the newest main commit. It was loaned to
Track A (Tab5-native RX audio out + binaural CW, see memory
project_rx_audio_track.md in the C:/dev/qmx-panadapter-audio
worktree) 2026-09-04, then reclaimed the SAME DAY for a batch of
main-branch feedback fixes (web pileup aging, decode-list layout
jump, WSPR PA-restore reliability) that needed a real bench before
going further. Track A's own session that evening also hit an
unresolved rpc_core/SDIO crash on this exact bench - see memory
project_20260904_sdio_wifi_crashes_audio_session.md - worth keeping
in mind if anything looks unstable here that main's own diff should
not cause. tree/branch below describe WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON IT, because
that is what 'bench flash dev' builds from. A stale entry here does
not read as wrong - it silently flashes the other tree's firmware
over this one and then PASSES the MAC verify, because the board is
the right board. Put dev back to Track A (C:/dev/qmx-panadapter-audio
+ feat/rx-audio-output) once these fixes are verified, or move Track
A to 'lab' if that is free by then.
benches.ip_note: DHCP, so it drifts - a convenience, not the authority. The board prints its own address at boot ('sta ip:' in its capture). qmx.local is NOT a discriminator: every unit answers to it, and on 2026-08-27 it resolved to a different board entirely.
benches.com_note: Was COM3 on the old laptop; re-verified by MAC (30:ED:A0:EA:DD:57) on the Ryzen box 2026-09-03, enumerated as COM5 there instead. COM follows the socket, not the board - re-check on any machine change.
benches.radio_note: Swapped 2026-09-05: was the small QMX. That radio's finals were worn down by WSPR TX at FULL power (110 s of key-down every 120 s) until it drew excessive current on plain RX; it is away being re-finalled. This is the real-world case the WSPR PA guard exists for - CLAUDE.md measures the finals at 4.69 W unguarded vs 1.12 W at the 6.0 V target. The QMX+ here reports 'QMX GPS source: QMX+ Internal' at CAT link-up and its second-tick phase-locks to SNTP within ~10 ms, so time_src reads GPS legitimately on this bench (NOT the #173 false-GPS case).

benches.name: field
benches.radio_note: Borrow the small QMX if a release touches radio behaviour.
benches.usb_flash_reason: This unit has never been USB-flashed. That provenance is what makes an OTA result credible - it is the only board that proves an update path a real user would take. Update it over the air only. If it must ever be recovered by USB, say so explicitly and update this field, because the OTA evidence resets with it.
